On the board-tick clock with the {{schedule_points}}-point schedule `saclac-census schedule` derives from that stock run, stock lands every point on its scheduled tick in two runs ({{stock_a_on_schedule}}, {{stock_b_on_schedule}}) whose census receipts are byte-identical ({{census_equal}}), and the time-services image lands every point on the same ticks ({{owned_on_schedule}}) while its instruction count since its origin differs from stock's at {{owned_offsets}} points. Both clocks restore the same post-boot checkpoint: stock {{stock_checkpoint}} ({{stock_checkpoint_lookup}} on the board-tick clock), created by the instruction-clock run as {{stock_checkpoint_created}}. Replayed without widening, the time-services image leaves {{raw_undebounced}} key releases undebounced before the next press and ends the DOWN sequence at cursor {{raw_cursor}} instead of {{expected_cursor}}.
scope: Emulation of stock X-M1 1.50 and the time-services tip image on the controlled-rtc run document under FujiMod 3d90035d, one route; tick ordinals count board ticks from each image's checkpoint, at board tick {{stock_origin_tick}} for stock and {{owned_origin_tick}} for the time-services image. notes: The unwidened replay fails because a stock instruction-clock run presses the next key as soon as stock has debounced the last one. Equal ticks do not give equal scanner phase: each image's scanner runs on its own timer history, so a press can still latch one scan interval apart (inferred, not measured here).
